question: Can a compiler written in the research data-machine language emit a residual program with a live dynamic input, for a declared subset of that same machine's instruction language, such that residual execution agrees with interpretation on both values and refusals?
level: Bounded construction and executed calibration of one declared transformation; no stable specializer, no general optimiser, no host-language compiler change and no self-hosting claim
imports: The source language is the declared subset used by the scaling preflight: input d, return s, two data slots, fixed length three
The interpreter is the subset interpreter generated by experiments/self_interpretation_scaling/check.py, reused unchanged at that length

The residual encoding is the same object-program encoding the compiler reads: a program node (tag 2) whose fields are instruction nodes, tag 0 input dst and tag 1 return src, with the instantiated program using two data registers
docs/research/futamura-projections-in-adva-terms.md states the projection and the observation policy this calibration uses
compiler_rule: Keep the last instruction that writes the returned slot, together with the return itself; drop every other instruction. A source program whose last instruction is not a return is refused by the compiler, with the refusal in its own source text.
observation: Run status and returned integer value. The trace is excluded on purpose, because compilation changes it.
protected: The machine is unchanged; no bound is widened and no operation is added
The interpreter is reused unchanged rather than rewritten for this calibration
The compiler is a program, not a host function, and it reads and writes the same declared program encoding
The source-to-residual rule is one sentence and every emitted residual is retained
Refusals count as observations: a source program that reads a slot nothing wrote must stay refused after compilation, not become a value
cases: all eight source programs input a, input b, return s over two slots
two dynamic values per program, 7 and 9
every residual instantiated into a real program and executed directly on the dynamic value
success: For all sixteen (program, dynamic value) pairs the interpreted and directly executed residual outcomes agree in status and value, including the two programs that must remain refused.
negative_controls: The compiler must refuse a source program outside the handled family, and that refusal is in the compiler's own source text rather than inferred
Two of the eight programs read a slot nothing wrote; both sides must refuse, so the calibration cannot pass by turning a refusal into a value
The residual is executed directly rather than through the interpreter, so its own semantics is what is measured
The compile cost is recorded beside the residual cost
exit: Stop at the first mismatch or resource limit; retain the failure and publish no positive claim from this attempt.
limits: The source language is a two-opcode, two-slot, fixed-length subset, and the compiler performs one declared transformation. Nothing here is a general optimiser, a stable specializer, a loader, or a self-hosting compiler, and projections two and three remain blocked by the bounds measured in the two self-interpretation preflights.
